title: Etale localization of algebraic-space strict transforms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. An effective Cartier divisor is a closed subspace whose ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor. For a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$, a morphism $g:Y\to T$, and $p:T^{\prime}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T\to T$, the strict transform of $Y$ means the closed subspace of $Y\times_TT^{\prime}$ cut out by the ideal of sections locally annihilated by some power of a local equation of the exceptional effective Cartier divisor $p^{-1}V(\mathcal K)$. Let $g:Y\to T$ be a morphism and let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal. Put $p:T^{\prime}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T\to T$ and let $Y^{\mathrm{st}}\hookrightarrow Y\times_TT^{\prime}$ be the strict transform just defined. Suppose $V\to T$ and $U\to Y$ are etale morphisms with $U,V$ schemes, and a scheme morphism $U\to V$ makes their square commute. Write $\mathcal K_V=\operatorname{im}(\mathcal K|_V\to\mathcal O_V)$ and $V^{\prime}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K_V}V$. Then $V^{\prime}\cong V\times_TT^{\prime}$ canonically, and $U\times_VV^{\prime}\to Y\times_TT^{\prime}$ is etale. Under these identifications the strict transform $U^{\mathrm{st}}$ of $U\to V$ is canonically $Y^{\mathrm{st}}\times_YU$ as a closed subspace of $U\times_VV^{\prime}$, compatibly with both projections. No quasi-compactness, separation, reducedness, or density hypothesis on $Y$ or $T$ is required.

proof.text: Use the sheaf fibre products of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The canonical isomorphism $U\times_V(V\times_TT^{\prime})\cong U\times_TT^{\prime}\cong (Y\times_TT^{\prime})\times_YU$ sends a compatible triple $(u,v,t^{\prime})$ to $(u,t^{\prime})$; its inverse inserts the given image of $u$ in $V$. These formulas are maps of sheaves and are inverse on every test scheme, so they preserve the projections to $U$, $Y$ and $T^{\prime}$. No cartesian assumption on the original square is used.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-strict-transform-etale-localization] with its $X=Y$, $f=g$, $A=V$, $W=U$, and with the same centre $\mathcal K$ and base $T$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given commutative square with schemes $U,V$ and etale horizontal maps. Its extended ideal $\mathcal K\mathcal O_V$ is the image $\mathcal K_V$ in this statement: both mean the ideal generated by the pulled-back sections. Its blowup is therefore the specified $V^{\prime}$. The cited statement gives the canonical isomorphism $V^{\prime}\cong V\times_TT^{\prime}$ over both factors, the etaleness of $U\times_VV^{\prime}\to Y\times_TT^{\prime}$, and the identification $U^{\mathrm{st}}\cong Y^{\mathrm{st}}\times_YU$. The strict-transform conventions agree: both divide the pulled-back structure sheaf by the sections killed locally by some power of the same exceptional equation. In particular the cited module clause for the structure sheaf gives this comparison compatibly with the quotient maps, so it is an identification as closed subspaces in the ambient fibre product of Step 1. The optional surjectivity clause of the cited theorem is not invoked.

The closed-subspace comparison in Step 2 lies over the ambient comparison in Step 1. Composing its closed immersion with the ambient projection to $U$ gives the strict-transform projection on either side, and composing with the ambient projection to $T^{\prime}$ gives the other projection. Thus the isomorphism has both required compatibilities. The application introduced no hypothesis of quasi-compactness, separation, reducedness or density: the reused theorem allows any morphism $f$ and any finite-type quasi-coherent centre.

lean.statement: theorem strictTransform_etale_locality {S : Scheme.{u}} {Y T V U : AlgebraicSpace S} (g : Y ⟶ T) (a : V ⟶ T) (w : U ⟶ Y) (f : U ⟶ V) (comm : w ≫ g = f ≫ a) (hV : ∃ V₀ : Over S, Nonempty (V.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj V₀)) (hU : ∃ U₀ : Over S, Nonempty (U.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj U₀)) (ha : IsEtale a.hom.hom) (hw : IsEtale w.hom.hom) (K : QuasiCoherentIdeal T) (hK : (K.val : T.Modules).IsFiniteType) (B : BlowupPresentation K) (P : StrictTransformPresentation g K B) : ∃ (KV : QuasiCoherentIdeal V) (k : (moduleTensorPullback a).obj (K.val : T.Modules) ⟶ (KV.val : V.Modules)), Epi k ∧ k ≫ KV.val.arrow = idealTensorMap a K ∧ ∃ (BV : BlowupPresentation KV) (PU : StrictTransformPresentation f KV BV) (v : BV.space ⟶ B.space) (h : PU.ambient ⟶ P.ambient), IsPullback BV.projection.hom v.hom a.hom B.projection.hom ∧ IsEtale h.hom.hom ∧ IsPullback h.hom PU.toSource.hom P.toSource.hom w.hom ∧ h ≫ P.toBlowup = PU.toBlowup ≫ v ∧ ∃ (j : PU.space ⟶ P.space), j ≫ P.inclusion = PU.inclusion ≫ h ∧ IsPullback j.hom (PU.inclusion ≫ PU.toSource).hom (P.inclusion ≫ P.toSource).hom w.hom
